overview: AlphaSense is an AI-powered market intelligence platform that combines proprietary search technology, generative AI workflows, and one of the largest collections of business content in the industry. Founded in 2011 by Jack Kokko and Raj Neervannan, the platform started as an AI search engine for financial documents and has evolved into a comprehensive research platform spanning document search, expert content, financial data, and autonomous AI research agents. The $930M acquisition of Tegus in July 2024 added a major expert transcript library and expert call services, making AlphaSense a direct competitor in the expert network space alongside its core document intelligence business.

history.narrative: AlphaSense was founded in 2011 by Jack Kokko (CEO) and Raj Neervannan (CTO), who met at Wharton. Kokko, originally from Oulu, Finland, conceived the idea while working as an investment banking analyst at Morgan Stanley, frustrated by the manual process of searching through thousands of PDFs. The company launched as an AI-powered search engine for financial research documents and grew through acquisitions (Stream in 2021, Sentieo in 2022) and organic growth, raising over $1.4B across multiple rounds. The transformative moment came in June 2024 with the $930M acquisition of Tegus (which also brought BamSEC and Canalyst), making AlphaSense a combined document intelligence and expert network platform. Notably, AlphaSense had previously sued both Sentieo and Tegus before acquiring them.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Calls
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one consultations with pre-vetted industry experts, inherited from Tegus's expert network infrastructure. Includes compliance training, recording, and transcript delivery. Experts go through onboarding, compliance vetting, and pre-call questionnaires before each call.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Insights (Tegus Transcript Library)
servicesDetailed.description: Library of 240,000+ expert call transcripts covering 27,000+ companies, growing at 8,000+ new transcripts per month. Acquired through Tegus. Every transcript undergoes multi-layered compliance review (AI-powered scanning plus human-in-the-loop). Public company transcripts published after 14-day delay; private company transcripts after 90-day delay.

servicesDetailed.name: Channel Checks (AI Interviewer)
servicesDetailed.description: AI-led expert interviews launched August 19, 2025. AlphaSense's autonomous AI Agent Interviewer conducts live 1:1 interviews with real market participants — distributors, suppliers, retailers — following structured guides with adaptive probing. Covers 350+ tickers across 20+ subsectors in TMT, Energy & Industrials, and Healthcare. Delivers raw transcripts within minutes and compliance-approved transcripts within hours.

servicesDetailed.name: Generative Search
servicesDetailed.description: Multi-agent research system that reasons across qualitative insights, structured financial data, and internal knowledge to deliver cited, auditable outputs. Built on AlphaSense's proprietary generative AI and the full 500M+ document library.

servicesDetailed.name: Deep Research
servicesDetailed.description: Launched June 10, 2025. Agentic AI mode within Generative Search that takes 10–30 minutes per query — autonomously plans research steps, searches across the full content library, iterates, and produces comprehensive reports (company primers, M&A screening, competitive landscapes, bull/bear debates). Users can filter by expert transcripts for focused output.

servicesDetailed.name: Generative Grid
servicesDetailed.description: Structured multi-question analysis tool that lets users compare themes, metrics, and expert views across multiple companies or transcripts in a grid format. Pre-built grids are available for Channel Checks insights.

servicesDetailed.name: Financial Data (via Canalyst)
servicesDetailed.description: Structured financials via Canalyst (acquired by Tegus, now part of AlphaSense) covering fully drivable models on 4,000+ public companies. Includes screening tools, industry-specific comparables, M&A transactions, funding rounds, valuation metrics, consensus estimates, and company-specific KPIs. Also includes BamSEC for self-serve SEC filing access.

servicesDetailed.name: Workflow Agents
servicesDetailed.description: Custom AI agents that users can build and deploy to automate recurring research tasks — company profiles, SWOT analysis, competitive landscapes, bull/bear debates, IPO primers. Includes a Slide Agent that creates pitchbook slides in a firm's own templates, plus Excel generation via Carousel Technologies (acquired Oct 2025).

servicesDetailed.name: Enterprise Intelligence
servicesDetailed.description: Allows organizations to connect shared drives, making internal memos, meeting notes, and slide decks searchable alongside AlphaSense's 500M+ external documents. Enterprise Intelligence deals grew 185% in 2025.

servicesDetailed.name: Monitoring & Alerts
servicesDetailed.description: Customized dashboards providing a single view of competitors, industry trends, and macro topics. Includes real-time alerts and mobile app access for tracking insights on the go.

aiPlatform.narrative: AlphaSense's AI capabilities are central to the platform and represent its primary competitive differentiation. The company has moved aggressively into agentic AI workflows, where autonomous agents conduct research, interview experts, and generate deliverables. The AI Agent Interviewer is the most distinctive capability — an autonomous conversational agent that conducts live 1:1 interviews with human experts, following structured guides while adapting dynamically to probe deeper. GenAI query usage increased 33% quarter-over-quarter as of late 2025, with exponential growth in LLM token consumption.

complianceExtended.narrative: AlphaSense operates a multi-layered compliance framework backed by 75+ dedicated compliance professionals and over $100M in annual investment in expert content. Every expert transcript undergoes AI-powered scanning for potential MNPI risks, followed by human-in-the-loop review. The process is overseen by CCO Brian Moroney (20+ years experience, former Goldman Sachs). Public company transcripts have a 14-day publication delay; private company transcripts have a 90-day delay. For AI-led Channel Checks, the AI Interviewer is tuned to avoid risky or inappropriate topics during live calls, and all transcripts go through the same compliance pipeline before publication.

complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: No major public regulatory actions against AlphaSense or its expert network operations were identified. AlphaSights filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against AlphaSense in January 2025 (SDNY), but this is a branding dispute, not a compliance issue. AlphaSense acquired Tegus's compliance infrastructure in the July 2024 acquisition and has integrated it into a unified framework.

clientFit.narrative: AlphaSense is best suited for organizations that need both document-level market intelligence and expert-sourced primary research in a single platform. Its strength is in combining quantitative financial data with qualitative expert content and AI-powered synthesis, making it especially powerful for buy-side research workflows. The platform is priced at $10K–$20K per seat annually, positioning it for mid-to-large enterprise budgets.

strengths: Largest integrated content library in the category (500M+ documents + 240K+ expert transcripts growing 8K+/month)
AI Agent Interviewer is a genuine first-mover product — no competitor offers autonomous AI-led expert calls at this scale
Deep institutional customer base (88% of S&P 100, 80% of top global banks, all 20 largest pharma companies)
Unified quantitative and qualitative research in one platform reduces tool fragmentation
$4B valuation with $1.4B+ raised from blue-chip investors (Viking, Goldman, CapitalG, SoftBank, J.P. Morgan)
caveats: Expert network capabilities are inherited from Tegus acquisition (July 2024) — integration of Tegus, Sentieo, BamSEC, Canalyst, and Carousel into one platform is complex; post-acquisition layoffs occurred Nov 2024
Claims 1M pre-qualified experts, but this is a marketing figure not independently verified; the expert network is newer than incumbents like GLG (25+ years) or AlphaSights
Emphasis on historical transcripts over tailored live expert conversations — PE firms may find expert insights don't fully align with current needs
Subscription pricing ($10K–$20K/seat) may be expensive for smaller firms or one-off research needs
The platform's breadth (documents + experts + financial data + AI agents) can create a steep learning curve
Channel Checks covers 20+ subsectors — narrower than traditional expert networks that serve any sector on demand
Rapid feature velocity means the product experience changes frequently; some users may find this disorienting
